newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, white metals rebound.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, white metals rebound.

text.p: New York precious metals ended mixed as white metals rebounded from recent selling, but gold and silver failed to hold on to their slim midsession gains and ended lower.

A dealer said the psychological impact of Switzerland's decision to sell gold to raise cash for a Holocaust fund was dampening sentiment, indicating yet another central bank with no qualms about selling yellow metal.
"Downward pressure is still there, but on the flip side we are at a level where worldwide demand is very strong and with bargain basement prices," the dealer added.
April gold settled 80 cents weaker at $353.60 an ounce, traded $355.30 to $353.00. Bullion was quoted after COMEX close at $351.90/$352.40 an ounce.
COMEX May silver settled 1.3 cents weaker at $5.227 an ounce, traded $5.30 to $5.13.

Analysts said the advance in palladium and platinum came from shortcovering after the market was heavily sold in recent sessions, though platinum pared some of its gains once gold began slipping midsession.
But the movements in precious metals were partly exaggerated by the modest volume, traders said.
Volume in gold and silver were estimated at 33,000 and 22,000 lots respectively.
April NYMEX platinum settled $2.20 higher at $386.30 an ounce, traded $389.00 to $383.00. June NYMEX palladium went out $6.50 firmer at $152.00 an ounce, off the day's high of $154.50.

On Thursday Standard Equities, part of Standard Bank, estimated that Russia had about 650,000 ounces of platinum in its stockpiles, enough to last 12 to 18 months if Russia is to maintain its current world supply level.
